parts.title: Hull Inspection Basics jan the cat

content.content: Walk the hull and deck. Look for cracks, crazing, blisters, and soft spots.

content: Check below waterline (if hauled)
Scan topsides for impact marks
Inspect deck around chainplates and stanchions

flashcards.title: Hull Inspection Basics jan the cat

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Hull Inspection Basics jan the cat'?

sideB.content: Walk the hull and deck. Look for cracks, crazing, blisters, and soft spots.

content.content: Examine gelcoat, non-skid, and hardware bedding to prevent leaks.

content: Non-skid wear
Lifeline stanchion bases
Toe-rail integrity

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Topsides & Deck'?

sideB.content: Examine gelcoat, non-skid, and hardware bedding to prevent leaks.

content.content: Confirm fair keel joint, tight bolts (if accessible), and smooth rudder travel.

content: Keel-hull joint (smiles)
Rudder play/bind
Weeps or staining

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Keel & Rudder Check'?

sideB.content: Confirm fair keel joint, tight bolts (if accessible), and smooth rudder travel.

content.content: Critical water ingress control points. Operate each valve, confirm smooth motion and full closure, inspect hoses, clamps, and backing pads.

content: Exercise and lube seacocks; replace frozen valves
Double-clamp below‑waterline hoses (opposing screw heads)
Carry tapered softwood plugs at each through‑hull

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Through‑Hulls & Seacocks'?

sideB.content: Critical water ingress control points. Operate each valve, confirm smooth motion and full closure, inspect hoses, clamps, and backing pads.

content.content: Assess structural connection. Look for weeping rust trails, cracking around the keel stub, and movement at the keel‑hull joint.

content: Torque-check bolts per builder spec (if accessible)
Mark witness lines across joint to detect movement
Document any 'smiles' or fairing cracks for monitoring

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Keel Bolts & Stub Inspection'?

sideB.content: Assess structural connection. Look for weeping rust trails, cracking around the keel stub, and movement at the keel‑hull joint.

content.content: Verify free, smooth helm with minimal play. Inspect upper/lower bearings and packing gland (or lip seal) for leaks or wear.

content: Check for vertical/lateral play at quadrant and heel
Grease or service bearings per manufacturer guidance
Inspect tiller head or quadrant fasteners and keyways

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Rudder Stock, Bearings & Gland'?

sideB.content: Verify free, smooth helm with minimal play. Inspect upper/lower bearings and packing gland (or lip seal) for leaks or wear.

content.content: Efficient propulsion depends on clean prop blades, true shaft, and a snug cutlass bearing.

content: Wiggle test at 6/12/3/9 o’clock—minimal play
Remove barnacles/coralline; avoid gouging bronze
Inspect shaft for scoring and straightness

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Propeller, Shaft & Cutlass Bearing'?

sideB.content: Efficient propulsion depends on clean prop blades, true shaft, and a snug cutlass bearing.

content.content: Primary shaft watertight seal. Confirm proper drip rate (packing) or dryness (mechanical seal) and secure clamps.

content: Packing gland: 1–3 drips/min under load (typical)
Mechanical seal: inspect bellows age and set screws
Check spare packing/mechanical seal kit aboard

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Shaft Seal / Stuffing Box'?

sideB.content: Primary shaft watertight seal. Confirm proper drip rate (packing) or dryness (mechanical seal) and secure clamps.

content.content: Aligns and supports the shaft. Inspect strut base, bolts, and bonding for cracks or movement.

content: Sight shaft alignment after haulout set
Confirm fairing around base is intact
Verify bonding/ground leads are secure

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Shaft Strut & Base'?

sideB.content: Aligns and supports the shaft. Inspect strut base, bolts, and bonding for cracks or movement.

content.content: Sacrificial anodes protect underwater metals. Replace when ~50% depleted and ensure tight, clean contact.

content: Prop, shaft, and hull plate anodes inspected
Check for stray current pitting and paint blisters
Record replacement dates in maintenance log

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Anodes (Zincs) & Corrosion Survey'?

sideB.content: Sacrificial anodes protect underwater metals. Replace when ~50% depleted and ensure tight, clean contact.

content.content: Speed/depth/fishfinder transducers must be clean and seated. Keep blanking plugs and caps ready aboard.

content: Remove marine growth; spin log wheel freely
Check O‑rings and retaining clips
Label cables and confirm data at the display

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Transducers & Blanking Plugs'?

sideB.content: Speed/depth/fishfinder transducers must be clean and seated. Keep blanking plugs and caps ready aboard.

content.content: Confirm exhaust mixing elbow discharges water and outlet is clear. Soot or salt buildup signals issues.

content: Look for steady water flow with engine running
Inspect outlet hose and clamps for heat or cracks
Verify anti‑siphon break function

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Exhaust Outlet (Wet) & Water Discharge'?

sideB.content: Confirm exhaust mixing elbow discharges water and outlet is clear. Soot or salt buildup signals issues.

content.content: Rapid drainage prevents cockpit flooding. Ensure hoses, seacocks, and strainers are clear and secure.

content: Flush drains; test for full flow
Inspect hose runs for low spots and kinks
Back plates sound, bolts tight and sealed

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Cockpit Scupper Through‑Hulls'?

sideB.content: Rapid drainage prevents cockpit flooding. Ensure hoses, seacocks, and strainers are clear and secure.

content.content: Structural and watertight seam. Inspect for gaps, loose fasteners, and impact damage along the rub rail.

content: Re‑bed sections showing leaks
Confirm fastener spacing and torque
Spot gelcoat cracking near fasteners

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Hull‑Deck Joint & Rub Rail'?

sideB.content: Structural and watertight seam. Inspect for gaps, loose fasteners, and impact damage along the rub rail.

content.content: Identify and log blisters below the waterline. Monitor for weeping, vinegar smell, or laminate softness.

content: Map blister fields and sizes
Open and rinse a sample to assess fluid
Plan repair: peel, dry, barrier‑coat as required

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Osmosis & Blister Survey'?

sideB.content: Identify and log blisters below the waterline. Monitor for weeping, vinegar smell, or laminate softness.

content.content: Look for stress crazing or leaks where chainplates pass through deck/hull. Water intrusion indicates hidden corrosion.

content: Inspect sealant at penetrations
Check for brown streaking or rust weeps
Verify tie‑rod/backing structure condition

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Chainplates & Hull‑Side Stress'?

sideB.content: Look for stress crazing or leaks where chainplates pass through deck/hull. Water intrusion indicates hidden corrosion.

content.content: Provides RF/lighting/engine bonding path. Ensure mechanical integrity and corrosion control.

content: Inspect Dynaplate/ground plate fasteners
Verify bonding lugs and continuity
Clean marine growth lightly

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Grounding Plate / Bonding Hardware'?

sideB.content: Provides RF/lighting/engine bonding path. Ensure mechanical integrity and corrosion control.

content.content: Swim ladder mounts, drain plugs, and fittings live hard lives. Keep sealed and tight to avoid water ingress.

content: Reseal loose fasteners and bedding
Confirm transom drains are clear
Check dinghy/tow eye and backing plates

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Transom Fittings & Drains'?

sideB.content: Swim ladder mounts, drain plugs, and fittings live hard lives. Keep sealed and tight to avoid water ingress.
